video_title: Giannis Trade Reaction, Lakers Fallout From Start Of Offseason + Live Q&A

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo traded to the Miami Heat in blockbuster deal
quotes.excerpt: Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis going to Miami and Tyler Herro, Caleb Martin, Jaime Jaquez Jr.
quotes.quote: The Giannis Antetokounmpo saga is over. Giannis has been traded to the Miami Heat for a big trade here. We got Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis going to Miami and Tyler Herro, Caleb Martin, Jaime Jaquez Jr., and three first-round picks, including the number 13 pick in the 2026 draft, as well as the future 2031 and 33 picks from the Heat, a pick swap in 2030, and a 2033 second-round pick.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers were rumored to be involved in Giannis trade talks
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers were rumored to be one of the potential teams in a three or four team
quotes.quote: The Lakers were rumored to be one of the potential teams in a three or four team Giannis trade because they could get involved, similar to what we saw earlier today with the Chicago Bulls, just taking on Nick Claxton for free. The Lakers could take on someone for free, or they could add in if Milwaukee likes but doesn't love Caleb Martin, the Lakers could potentially offer them a first-round pick for Caleb Martin or a pick and something else.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Jaylen Brown's trade offer to the Heat's Giannis package
quotes.excerpt: Between the two offers of Jaylen Brown and two future firsts from Boston compared to this trade offer
quotes.quote: Between the two offers of Jaylen Brown and two future firsts from Boston compared to this trade offer from the Heat, I thought it was close, but I did lean on the Heat side for a number of reasons. Number one, they are offering the number 13 pick, which already is a lottery pick. There is no guarantee that the future Boston picks become a lottery pick. There is no guarantee that the future Heat picks become a lottery pick.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo's long-term outlook in Miami
quotes.excerpt: Giannis is going to be 36 and he is someone that has struggled with injuries over the last
quotes.quote: Giannis is going to be 36 and he is someone that has struggled with injuries over the last few years and has not been healthy to close multiple seasons, to say nothing of where Bam Adebayo will be at that point. Miami has an extended history here of fielding successful contenders and finding ways to revamp and find the next star and they have been doing this for 30 years now at this point, or close to it, since Pat Riley got involved.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Caleb Martin's potential as an offseason target for the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: Caleb Martin is one guy that I've watched a ton of film on and the upside is there.
quotes.quote: Caleb Martin is one guy that I've watched a ton of film on and the upside is there. There is some of the Christian Wood, Deandre Ayton motor stuff with him where you see the talent, you see the production, but he hasn't quite put it together. He clashed with Eric Spoelstra this past season, which is not a good look for any young player and ten out of ten times you're going to take Eric Spoelstra's side in that just based on who he is as a coach, his stature, his character.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Caleb Martin's impressive performance in limited minutes
quotes.excerpt: Caleb Martin played 10 games this past season where he played 30 plus minutes. In those 10 games
quotes.quote: Caleb Martin played 10 games this past season where he played 30 plus minutes. In those 10 games, he averaged 18 points per game, 14 rebounds, three blocks, and one steal. This dude is a beast and from a per-possession basis, you see the numbers, but some guys you can extrapolate things out. We've seen what Caleb Martin can do in a bigger role.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Ike Anigbogu's new five-year contract with the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: I would assume Ike Anigbogu ends up signing a five-year $112 million deal. I think that's a fair deal
quotes.quote: I would assume Ike Anigbogu ends up signing a five-year $112 million deal. I think that's a fair deal. It's higher than a lot of people were projecting. I saw a lot of people saying, is he going to get like 16 million, 18 million, 19 million? I had been saying I thought he was going to be in the low to mid 20s. This ends up netting out at about 22.4 AAV, so that's in line with my opinion of his value and I think that's a fair deal for both sides.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves, Bulls, and Nets trade details and salary cap impact
quotes.excerpt: The Timberwolves ended up sending Julius Randle and the number 28 pick in a cost-cutting move to
quotes.quote: The Timberwolves ended up sending Julius Randle and the number 28 pick in a cost-cutting move to the Nets. Then the Nets sent Nick Claxton to the Bulls who took him into their cap space and the Wolves acquired the number 33 pick and ended up saving tens of millions of dollars in luxury tax bill, although they then turned around and signed Ike Anigbogu and they are still now have this $33 million trade exception which they could acquire players into that.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Dewayne Dedmon's multi-year contract signing
quotes.excerpt: Dewayne Dedmon signed a multi-year 10 plus million dollar deal.
quotes.quote: Dewayne Dedmon signed a multi-year 10 plus million dollar deal. It's interesting, we don't have the official number on that in terms of years or money, but I thought that was a fine deal, locking him up long-term.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Trae Young's four-year contract extension and market value
quotes.excerpt: Trae Young signed a four-year $212 million extension. He got a raise off of his $49 million player option
quotes.quote: Trae Young signed a four-year $212 million extension. He got a raise off of his $49 million player option, which I was pretty surprised by just based on his recent performance the last few years, his lack of trade value. He does not have trade value right now. I don't think he has a lot of value in general around the league unless it's a bad team just looking to be relevant and maybe sell some tickets.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Thunder trade Aaron Wiggins to the Hawks for two second-round picks
quotes.excerpt: The Thunder ended up trading Aaron Wiggins to the Hawks for two second-round picks
quotes.quote: The Thunder ended up trading Aaron Wiggins to the Hawks for two second-round picks, which was the Hawks' 2030 second-round pick and the least favorable of the Hawks and Lakers' second-round picks in 2032. So the Thunder did their first move to save some money and it's what I suspected in terms of they had to get off of Isaiah Hartenstein or Lou Dort, but once you actually looked at their cap sheet, they could easily just get off Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe and get duck and save a bunch of money that way.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Goodwin and C.J. McCollum's contract extensions
quotes.excerpt: Jordan Goodwin resigned three-year $19 million deal. I thought that was kind of low
quotes.quote: Jordan Goodwin resigned three-year $19 million deal. I thought that was kind of low and I think that's a good thing for the Lakers and just the overall free agent market. To me, Goodwin is more of an eight to $10 million player, but if he's making $6 million, that's a sign of the market and things squeezing a little bit. C.J. McCollum one-year $21 million extension.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Collin Gillespie's four-year contract with the Suns
quotes.excerpt: Collin Gillespie four-year $48 million deal to return to Phoenix.
quotes.quote: Collin Gillespie four-year $48 million deal to return to Phoenix. I thought that was a bit low as well. I thought he was going to be someone that would be going closer to the non-taxpayer MLE.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' offseason strategy and roster needs
quotes.excerpt: There's been some positive developments for the Lakers and some negative developments for the Lakers
quotes.quote: There's been some positive developments for the Lakers and some negative developments for the Lakers. I want to read through these. Positive developments for the Lakers, I think Goodwin and Gillespie getting the prices that they got are good for the Lakers keeping some of their principal role players. If we put Goodwin as an analog here at 6 million and Gillespie at 12 million, I think that probably means Marcus Smart is probably closer to 10 million.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' first move and roster construction
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers' first move is going to tell us a lot about what their plans are.
quotes.quote: The Lakers' first move is going to tell us a lot about what their plans are. Because for example, if the Lakers extend Rui Hachimura, then that means that's either a chunk of their cap space immediately gone, although I would assume Rui is making less than his cap hold. But still, when you're talking about the cap space, you are rescinding Rui's rights. So that's a chunk of your cap space gone, or that signals that they are I think more likely going over the cap and using the non-taxpayer MLE, or if they go under the cap, it also doesn't matter because they are going to make their moves and then sign Austin Reaves.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' potential trade for a starting center
quotes.excerpt: I really think they need a center and that was clear in that story from ESPN
quotes.quote: I really think they need a center and that was clear in that story from ESPN of like, Luka wants an A-list center, Luka wants the lob threat, Luka wants it's like center and shooting. Now, I think you'd like to see Luka also want some defense and athleticism. I think those are a couple things that I'm sure he wants as well, but like weren't explicitly stated. It's more than just the offensive end. It's more than just having the lob threat and the shooting. I think the Lakers need a lot of other things as well.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' center options and trade possibilities
quotes.excerpt: There are certainly guys like a Walker Kessler or Jalen Duren or Derrick Lively that I would
quotes.quote: There are certainly guys like a Walker Kessler or Jalen Duren or Derrick Lively that I would clearly rather have than Nick Claxton. If it ends up Robert Williams or Mitchell Robinson or running it back with Deandre Ayton, I would much rather just have Nick Claxton who I think is better than all those guys, but is also healthier than all those guys. He's basically been 70 plus games the last four years, where all of those guys, I mean more so Robinson and Williams, have dealt with extensive injury histories and are basically guys who, for as much as I love Robert Williams, he's one of my favorite bang for your buck options at the center spot.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' center rotation and potential trade targets
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers are running out of center options. There's Walker Kessler or in Jalen Duren or Derrick Lively
quotes.quote: The Lakers are running out of center options. There's Walker Kessler or in Jalen Duren or Derrick Lively that I would clearly rather have than Nick Claxton. If it ends up Robert Williams or Mitchell Robinson or running it back with Deandre Ayton, I would much rather just have Nick Claxton who I think is better than all those guys, but is also healthier than all those guys. He's basically been 70 plus games the last four years, where all of those guys, I mean more so Robinson and Williams, have dealt with extensive injury histories and are basically guys who, for as much as I love Robert Williams, he's one of my favorite bang for your buck options at the center spot.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' potential trade for a starting center
quotes.excerpt: I would like AD on a buyout. I would not want to give up or pay AD whatever
quotes.quote: I would like AD on a buyout. I would not want to give up or pay AD whatever he's about to be making 50 almost $60 million. I think that's a very high number for a guy that you just don't have guarantees will be healthy. I go to OKC, I don't see I-Hart, not Wemby, not Chet, obviously, not Kat. I you don't have enough to get Shai. And I some of those guys I don't even love the fit with what the Lakers have. But like just going down the center list, it's like they're running out of options and I don't know who it is and like I've been working on the center target list and going through film on a bunch of these guys and going through the numbers on a bunch of these guys and it's like already I crossed off I don't see Isaiah Hartenstein becoming available.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' offseason plans for Austin Reaves and Rui Hachimura
quotes.excerpt: I think Marcus is the one where they probably have to use an exception and that exception will show you what the Lakers' plans are.
quotes.quote: If I had to guess, when/what is Lakers first move? I think Marcus is the one where they probably have to use an exception and that exception will show you what the Lakers' plans are. Luke is also another one where they could potentially use a room exception or bird rights, and then either way, if it's room exception, that means they're going under the cap using cap space. If it's bird rights, they're going above the cap, and that means they are going to be an over-the-cap team.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers likely to re-sign Austin Reaves
quotes.excerpt: If my theory that the Lakers have agreed to something with Austin is right, maybe we get the Austin news here at some point.
quotes.quote: If my theory that the Lakers have agreed to something with Austin is right, maybe we get the Austin news here at some point in the next 24 to 48 hours of the Lakers and Austin Reaves have agreed to a five-year, X million dollar deal, but they will not be signing it until the Lakers make their other moves. They will be retaining Austin on his cap hold and then sign him at a future date. That might make the most sense of the next 24 to 48 hours.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' priority is to re-sign Austin Reaves and D'Angelo Russell
quotes.excerpt: The big one here to me is Rui and if they extend him, because that again, likely signals they're going above the cap.
quotes.quote: The big one here to me is Rui and if they extend him, because that again, likely signals they're going above the cap if they end up doing that. Then obviously there's LeBron and his future, which I don't know when we're going to be getting the clarity on that and whether they are rescinding his rights or whether he's immediately re-signing and what that number's at, and how contingent is it on LA's other moves in terms of whether he's back or what number he's back at. There's a lot of moving parts with that. If I had to guess, I would say Austin probably because I think in terms of priority, it's Austin and LeBron at the top.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's trade availability and Boston's conservative approach
quotes.excerpt: I think Boston operates a little bit more conservatively in general and I don't think they've burned that bridge.
quotes.quote: I think Boston operates a little bit more conservatively in general and I don't think they've burned that bridge. There have been plenty of times where guys get offered up and then you do have to repair the bridge, and the bridge might be burned, but you can still rebuild the bridge. There's enough history there, he's won a championship there, he's won a Finals MVP there, he is coming off of a career year, but he's also been making some weird decisions post-season in terms of his Twitch streams and his comments, and I would say that that has indicated to me that's a guy who probably wants out of Boston and I believe there was a report over the last couple days that Jaylen Brown was open to being traded.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential trade packages for Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: The three guys they have considered trading Jaylen Brown for are Kawhi Leonard, Kevin Durant, and Giannis Antetokounmpo.
quotes.quote: The three guys they have considered trading Jaylen Brown for are Kawhi Leonard, Kevin Durant, and Giannis Antetokounmpo. It's been a pretty high bar to potentially trade Jaylen Brown. So, if it is burned and if he does ask out, I think they're going to want a haul. So, earlier I mentioned if you're looking at the Boston-Milwaukee trade and them potentially expanding that out from the Milwaukee side, maybe Milwaukee's like, we're getting the two picks, we're getting off Giannis's contract, maybe we're adding in Portis or we're adding in Kuzma, whatever the situation is, so we're saving some money, we're getting a couple Boston picks, but now we want to reroute Jaylen Brown. So maybe we reroute him to Portland, get our picks back and get like an interesting young player, or we reroute him to the Lakers, we don't even have to take anything back from the Lakers, but you know, it's sort of the theoretical Giannis trade that the Lakers could have offered them of, get out of jail free, get off the contract and we'll send you picks.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' cap flexibility and potential pursuit of Walker Kessler
quotes.excerpt: If the Lakers go 48-52 million in cap space, you could get very aggressive with Kessler.
quotes.quote: If the Lakers go 48-52 million in cap space, you could get very aggressive with Kessler and have like a giant first-year offer that then declines from there. But that's I guess one way to to try to twist their arm. I think the more likely way, like I just think if you're Utah, you have to match almost anything. The way to get to the 20% is if you blow them away with a sign-and-trade. And also look, I think the hoop collective guys are some of the best in the business and I know all those guys personally, have great relationships with each of them, but of course, as I said earlier in the show, like right now, there's a lot of agendas going around, there's a lot of intel going around, and maybe from the Utah side, they're leaking this, they want this out there of, we're keeping Kessler actually and like, if you want Kessler, you got to blow us away with an offer.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler's fit with the Lakers compared to DeAndre Ayton
quotes.excerpt: Walker Kessler checks every box that the Lakers need from the center spot, checks every box in direct comparison with the DeAndre Ayton.
quotes.quote: Walker Kessler checks every box that the Lakers need from the center spot, checks every box in direct comparison with the DeAndre Ayton. He's a better lob threat, he's a better finisher, he's a better rebounder, he's a better rim protector, he's a better overall defender, much better defensive anchor. I think he's someone that has the upside to be defensive player of the year, all-defense level guy, like I guess non-Wemby division, because Wemby's going to be leading that for the next decade, but also top five, you can lead the league in field goal percentage allowed, he's already been in that mix. He could also be a guy who's both a top five rebounder and top five rim protector. It's very hard to find someone of that ilk. On paper, Jalen Duren is a better player, he was an All-Star, he made 13 All-NBA, and he's probably going to make more money than Walker Kessler. At the same time, for what the Lakers specifically need, I think Walker Kessler is a better fit because he's bigger than Duren, he's they're close in rebounding, but Kessler, at least if you go by his numbers, sans the the five-game season, slightly better rebounder and definitely a better defender.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' potential interest in Kyle Kuzma and other trade targets
quotes.excerpt: I would take Ware in a heartbeat, though I am a little concerned with like going all in on him as like your starting center.
quotes.quote: I would take Ware in a heartbeat, though I am a little concerned with like going all in on him as like your starting center. I think at that point, a semi-realistic thing to me would be like could you go get Ware and then sign the Williams or Robinson so you do have some insurance like and keep Jackson, so you have some insurance. Where is your long-term center? You have the Williams or Robinson veteran backup option if Ware just isn't ready or like whatever, you could also close sometimes with those guys and then you also have Jackson, you have this three-headed committee. Kuzma, I know he holds a special place in Lakers fans' hearts, but 19.4 million expiring, there are worse contracts. I think he's currently a below non-taxpayer mid-level guy, he's coming off, I just want to be accurate here with his shooting numbers, but did have some pretty rough games the last couple of years in particular. I think has regressed.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Jovan Buha's assessment of D'Angelo Russell's performance
quotes.excerpt: I think the aesthetic of his game has changed a lot going from LA to Washington to eventually Milwaukee and that part's been hard.
quotes.quote: I think the aesthetic of his game has changed a lot going from LA to Washington to eventually Milwaukee and that part's been hard. You look at the playoffs, they weren't in the playoffs this past year, but go back two years ago, in the playoffs, averaged six points, two rebounds, 2.7 assists, shot 34% and 20% on threes, played 20 minutes a night and was progressively played out of that series. I don't know, I I don't love Kuzma at 19. Like I'd rather just have Rui at 17 than Kuzma at 19. Even if Kuzma's better defender, but Rui's a much better shooter and I think at this point, overall offensive player. So, yeah, I mean, Kuzma's got the bag and he'll always have that, but it's not it's not been the best few years for Kuz in terms of his actual like value and production.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' potential trade targets for the 25th pick
quotes.excerpt: If the Lakers are trading up, I talked about this on Lakers Collective, Moises Johnson Jr., Cameron Carr, or Dalen Terry would be guys I'd be looking at to trade up for.
quotes.quote: If the Lakers are trading up, I talked about this on Lakers Collective, Moises Johnson Jr., Cameron Carr, or Dalen Terry would be guys I'd be looking at to trade up for, or Quinton, depending on the pick that you're trading up for. At 25, I think Quinton or Zubi, I'd be open to trading up for either one of those guys, Quinton or Swayne, would be a dream if I'm the Lakers, and then you're basically getting Robert Williams for a quarter of the price and also 10 years younger, and with similar injury concerns, but still with the upside to potentially reach the the peak that that Robert Williams never reached, or only reached in flashes, I think particularly in Boston.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler's contract value in the current NBA market
quotes.excerpt: Kessler at 30 or 32 million is more in line with Hartenstein getting his previous contract
quotes.quote: I understand why the notion of paying someone 30 million plus who can't even average 20 points a game is kind of crazy. But I also think with the cap moving the way that it is, I would almost say, when we have the Austin conversation, which I don't really want to dive into, but I'm bringing it up, so I'm kind of doing this to myself. If we say even like 35 million for Austin, and you look at some of the guys in that mid-30s, I think he's better than most of those guys. I think there's a couple of guys who are clearly better than him, maybe a couple of guys on his level, and then I think there's several guys he's better than. I would even say right now 35 million is more like 32 million a couple years ago. If you look at just the general inflation with contracts, the rising cap, what percentage of the cap it is, it's closer to like 32 million. So, Kessler at 30 or 32 million is more in line with Hartenstein getting his previous contract in the mid-to-high 20s. I just think contracts are rising.
